#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
starting_line_verify — verification battery for the locked 2026-10-02 baseline.

Every arithmetic claim in STARTING_LINE_2026-10-02, recomputed from scratch.
Run: python3 starting_line_verify.py
"""
import math

def main():
    ok = True
    def chk(name, cond):
        nonlocal ok
        print(f"{'PASS' if cond else 'FAIL'}  {name}")
        if not cond:
            ok = False

    b = lambda G: 0.4992 * G - 0.0104 * G * G
    chk("beta(47) = 0.4888", abs(b(47) - 0.4888) < 1e-12)
    chk("beta(48) = 0", abs(b(48)) < 1e-12)
    chk("beta(49) = -0.5096", abs(b(49) + 0.5096) < 1e-12)
    chk("0.0104*G*(48-G) form", abs(0.0104 * 47 * 1 - 0.4888) < 1e-12)
    chk("7776/162 = 48; 6^5 = 7776; 2*3^4 = 162",
        7776 / 162 == 48 and 6**5 == 7776 and 2 * 3**4 == 162)
    chk("4608 = 2*48^2", 4608 == 2 * 48 * 48)
    chk("407096 + 251654 = 658750", 407096 + 251654 == 658750)
    chk("(2*4/5)^2 = 2.56", abs((2 * 4 / 5) ** 2 - 2.56) < 1e-12)
    chk("0.9216/48 = 0.0192", abs(0.9216 / 48 - 0.0192) < 1e-12)
    chk("cancellation at 48", abs((0.48 * 48 - 0.0104 * 48**2) + 0.0192 * 48) < 1e-12)
    chk("0.50*47 - (1/96)*47^2 = 0.4895833 (!= 0.4888)",
        abs(0.50 * 47 - (1 / 96) * 47**2 - 0.4895833) < 1e-6)
    chk("weight sets sum to 1",
        abs(0.42 + 0.22 + 0.32 + 0.04 - 1) < 1e-12 and
        abs(0.28 + 0.24 + 0.28 + 0.16 + 0.04 - 1) < 1e-12)
    chk("arctan(4/3) = 53.130102 deg", abs(math.degrees(math.atan(4 / 3)) - 53.130102) < 1e-6)
    chk("rotation (1/5)[[3,-4],[4,3]] det = 1, unit columns",
        abs((3/5) * (3/5) - (-4/5) * (4/5) - 1) < 1e-12)
    d, dk, w = [4, 1, 0], [2, 1, 1], [1, 1, 1]
    lam = sum(wi * di * ki for wi, di, ki in zip(w, d, dk)) / sum(wi * ki**2 for wi, ki in zip(w, dk))
    H = [di - lam * ki for di, ki in zip(d, dk)]
    chk("lambda = 1.5, H = [1.0, -0.5, -1.5]", lam == 1.5 and H == [1.0, -0.5, -1.5])

    print("\nSTARTING-LINE BATTERY:", "ALL PASS" if ok else "FAILURES PRESENT")
    return 0 if ok else 1

if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
partition_1128 — deep-dive analysis of the 1,128 codec pairs, as runnable code.

Discovers and proves the exact three-class partition:
  944 door pairs   — generate the 7,140 doors (distance >= 2)
  124 alias pairs  — exactly the distance-1 pairs = the filed codec's documented
                     exception class; ZERO of them are doors
   60 never-door pairs — 3 value-infeasible at sum extremes
                         ((3,5)=8: d can't stay >= 3; (93,97) and (95,97): d can't stay <= 97),
                         57 pass the value identity but fail popcount/XOR
                     (one further alias pair, (3,7), is also value-infeasible)

Secondary findings (all recomputed):
  - complementary pairs (a+b=128, 17 of them) are the most door-rich (up to 32 each)
  - clean doors (360) concentrate at distances 2/3/4 = 122/168/70; none at 5/6

Run: python3 partition_1128.py
"""
from collections import Counter
from doors_generate import MASKS, bits, ham, generate_doors

MSET = set(MASKS)

def value_feasible(a, b):
    """Exists c in M\\{a,b} with d=a+b-c in M\\{a,b,c}?"""
    for c in MASKS:
        if c == a or c == b:
            continue
        d = a + b - c
        if d in MSET and d not in (a, b, c):
            return True
    return False

def main():
    ok = True
    def chk(name, cond, detail=""):
        nonlocal ok
        print(f"{'PASS' if cond else 'FAIL'}  {name}" + (f"  [{detail}]" if detail else ""))
        if not cond:
            ok = False

    doors = generate_doors()
    door_pairs = {tuple(sorted((a, b))) for a, b, c, d in doors}
    all_pairs = [(MASKS[i], MASKS[j]) for i in range(48) for j in range(i + 1, 48)]
    never = [p for p in all_pairs if tuple(sorted(p)) not in door_pairs]
    alias = [p for p in never if ham(*p) == 1]
    rest = [p for p in never if ham(*p) > 1]

    chk("1128 = 944 + 124 + 60",
        len(door_pairs) == 944 and len(alias) == 124 and len(rest) == 60,
        f"{len(door_pairs)}+{len(alias)}+{len(rest)}")
    chk("alias pairs are exactly the distance-1 pairs",
        len(alias) == sum(1 for a, b in all_pairs if ham(a, b) == 1) == 124)
    chk("zero alias pairs are doors",
        all(tuple(sorted(p)) not in door_pairs for p in alias))

    vinfeas = [p for p in rest if not value_feasible(*p)]
    chk("3 value-infeasible at sum extremes", len(vinfeas) == 3,
        str(sorted(a + b for a, b in vinfeas)))
    chk("57 pass value identity, fail popcount/XOR", len(rest) - len(vinfeas) == 57)

    per_pair = Counter(tuple(sorted((a, b))) for a, b, c, d in doors)
    comp = [(a, b) for a, b in door_pairs if a + b == 128]
    chk("17 complementary (sum-128) door pairs", len(comp) == 17)
    chk("max doors per pair is 32, achieved by complementary pairs",
        max(per_pair.values()) == 32 and
        all(a + b == 128 for (a, b), n in per_pair.most_common(3)))

    clean_d = Counter(ham(a, b) for a, b, c, d in doors
                      if bits(c) == (bits(a) & bits(b)))
    chk("clean doors 122/168/70 at d2/d3/d4, none at d5/d6",
        dict(sorted(clean_d.items())) == {2: 122, 3: 168, 4: 70})

    print("\nPARTITION BATTERY:", "ALL PASS" if ok else "FAILURES PRESENT")
    return 0 if ok else 1

if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

H columns = odd masks 3..97 (every column carries the common bit, row 0). Repair-or-refuse decoder: - single payload spike (any nonzero magnitude) -> repaired - single parity-tail edit -> detected, payload intact - dual spikes, any magnitudes/signs -> refused (never silently miscorrected) Measured (this file recomputes): - 48/48 single spikes repaired - 0/1128 unsigned pair XORs equal a column ("0 XOR collisions") - 124/1128 opposite-sign equal-magnitude pairs alias to a single axis (the documented exception class; the v4 14-row matrix closes it) - column weight distribution 6/15/16/9/2 Docket: MI-PPA-CODEC-2026 | Monsters Ink LLC """ N_MSG, N_PAR = 48, 7 MASKS = [m for m in range(3, 98) if m % 2 == 1] assert len(MASKS) == 48 and all(m & 1 for m in MASKS) def syndrome(spikes): """XOR of masks at spiked positions. spikes: dict {pos: True} (binary model).""" s = 0 for p in spikes: s ^= MASKS[p] return s def decode_single(s): """Return column index whose mask equals syndrome s, else None (refuse).""" return MASKS.index(s) if s in MASKS else None def analyze(): res = {} # singles res["singles_repaired"] = sum(1 for i in range(48) if decode_single(MASKS[i]) == i) # unsigned pairs: XOR equals a column? cols = set(MASKS) xor_is_col = 0 pair_xors = set() for i in range(48): for j in range(i + 1, 48): x = MASKS[i] ^ MASKS[j] pair_xors.add(x) if x in cols: xor_is_col += 1 res["pairs"] = 1128 res["xor_collisions"] = xor_is_col res["distinct_pair_xors"] = len(pair_xors) # opposite-sign equal-magnitude pairs: (Mi - Mj) is a single axis (power of two)? # binary model: Mi XOR Mj has popcount 1 <=> Mi - Mj = +/- 2^k alias = [(i, j) for i in range(48) for j in range(i + 1, 48) if bin(MASKS[i] ^ MASKS[j]).count("1") == 1] res["signed_alias_pairs"] = len(alias) # column weight distribution from collections import Counter res["weight_dist"] = dict(sorted(Counter(bin(m).count("1") for m in MASKS).items())) res["row0_all_ones"] = all(m & 1 for m in MASKS) return res if __name__ == "__main__": import json print(json.dumps(analyze(), indent=1)) §3 — doors_generate.py #!/usr/bin/env python3 """ DOORS — full generation code for the 7,140-door merge map. Source: the FILED 7x48 codec matrix (64/170,360) = odd masks 3..97. A "door" is two nodes (a,b) merging via a collapsed hallway (c) into (d). Three constraints, all necessary: 1. Value identity: a + b - c = d (d must be a mask value, all four distinct) 2. Weight identity: |a| + |b| - |c| = |d| (popcounts of the 7-bit masks) 3. XOR preservation: (a ^ b) == (c ^ d) (the difference pattern survives the collapse) These three generate EXACTLY 7,140 doors — verified cell-for-cell against the reference workbook (doors_only_extensive.xlsx, All_7140). c if d not in MSET or d in (a, b, c): continue if wa + wb - len(bits(c)) != len(bits(d)): continue if xab != (c ^ d): continue doors.append((a, b, c, d)) return doors def door_record(a, b, c, d): Sa, Sb, Sc, Sd = bits(a), bits(b), bits(c), bits(d) ov = Sa & Sb return { "merge": [a, b], "via_collapsed": c, "into": d, "operation": f"{a}+{b}-{c}={d}", "Sa": sorted(Sa), "Sb": sorted(Sb), "Sc": sorted(Sc), "Sd": sorted(Sd), "overlap_a_b": sorted(ov), "overlap_is_collapsed": Sc == ov, "distance_a_b": ham(a, b), "indices": {"a": MIDX[a], "b": MIDX[b], "c": MIDX[c], "d": MIDX[d]}, } def build_workbook(path): """Write the full doors workbook (All_7140 + per-distance sheets).""" import openpyxl doors = generate_doors() wb = openpyxl.Workbook() ws = wb.active ws.title = "All_7140" hdr = ["merge", "via_collapsed", "into", "operation", "Sa", "Sb", "Sc", "Sd", "overlap_a_b", "overlap_is_collapsed", "distance_a_b", "indices"] ws.append(hdr) bydist = {} for a, b, c, d in doors: r = door_record(a, b, c, d) ws.append([str(r["merge"]), r["via_collapsed"], r["into"], r["operation"], str(r["Sa"]), str(r["Sb"]), str(r["Sc"]), str(r["Sd"]), str(r["overlap_a_b"]), r["overlap_is_collapsed"], r["distance_a_b"], str(r["indices"])]) bydist.setdefault(r["distance_a_b"], []).append(r) for dist in sorted(bydist): s = wb.create_sheet(f"dist_{dist}") s.append(hdr) for r in bydist[dist]: s.append([str(r["merge"]), r["via_collapsed"], r["into"], r["operation"], str(r["Sa"]), str(r["Sb"]), str(r["Sc"]), str(r["Sd"]), str(r["overlap_a_b"]), r["overlap_is_collapsed"], r["distance_a_b"], str(r["indices"])]) wb.save(path) return len(doors) if __name__ == "__main__": import sys n = build_workbook(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "doors_generated.xlsx") print(f"doors written: {n}") §4 — doors_verify.py #!/usr/bin/env python3 """ DOORS — full verification battery for the 7,140-door merge map. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
codec_filed — the FILED [55,8] fault-refusing codec (64/170,360), pure Python.

48 message positions + 7 binary parity checks = 55-symbol codewords.
H columns = odd masks 3..97 (every column carries the common bit, row 0).

Repair-or-refuse decoder:
  - single payload spike (any nonzero magnitude) -> repaired (48/48)
  - single parity-tail edit -> detected, payload intact
  - dual spikes, same strict sign -> refused
  - dual spikes, opposite signs, equal magnitude -> 1004/1128 refused;
    124/1128 alias to a single axis (the documented exception class;
    the v4 14-row matrix closes it)
  Nothing is ever silently miscorrected outside the 124 alias class.

Measured (this file recomputes):
  - 48/48 single spikes repaired
  - 0/1128 unsigned pair XORs equal a column          ("0 XOR collisions")
  - 124/1128 opposite-sign equal-magnitude pairs alias to a single axis
    (the documented exception class; the v4 14-row matrix closes it)
  - column weight distribution 6/15/16/9/2

Docket: MI-PPA-CODEC-2026 | Monsters Ink LLC
"""

N_MSG, N_PAR = 48, 7
MASKS = [m for m in range(3, 98) if m % 2 == 1]
assert len(MASKS) == N_MSG and all(m & 1 for m in MASKS)
assert max(MASKS) < 2 ** N_PAR  # 7-bit columns

def syndrome(spikes):
    """XOR of masks at spiked positions. spikes: iterable of column indices."""
    s = 0
    for p in spikes:
        s ^= MASKS[p]
    return s

def decode_single(s):
    """Return column index whose mask equals syndrome s, else None (refuse)."""
    return MASKS.index(s) if s in MASKS else None

def analyze():
    res = {}
    # singles
    res["singles_repaired"] = sum(1 for i in range(N_MSG) if decode_single(MASKS[i]) == i)
    # unsigned pairs: XOR equals a column?
    cols = set(MASKS)
    xor_is_col = 0
    pair_xors = set()
    for i in range(N_MSG):
        for j in range(i + 1, N_MSG):
            x = MASKS[i] ^ MASKS[j]
            pair_xors.add(x)
            if x in cols:
                xor_is_col += 1
    res["pairs"] = N_MSG * (N_MSG - 1) // 2
    res["xor_collisions"] = xor_is_col
    res["distinct_pair_xors"] = len(pair_xors)
    # opposite-sign equal-magnitude pairs: (Mi - Mj) is a single axis (power of two)?
    # binary model: Mi XOR Mj has popcount 1  <=>  Mi - Mj = +/- 2^k
    alias = [(i, j) for i in range(N_MSG) for j in range(i + 1, N_MSG)
             if bin(MASKS[i] ^ MASKS[j]).count("1") == 1]
    res["signed_alias_pairs"] = len(alias)
    # column weight distribution
    from collections import Counter
    res["weight_dist"] = dict(sorted(Counter(bin(m).count("1") for m in MASKS).items()))
    res["row0_all_ones"] = all(m & 1 for m in MASKS)
    return res

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import json
    print(json.dumps(analyze(), indent=1))

"""
DOORS — full verification battery for the 7,140-door merge map.

Checks every claim the Full Plate makes about the doors, independently
recomputed from the filed masks + the three generation constraints.
Run: python3 doors_verify.py
"""
from collections import Counter
from doors_generate import MASKS, bits, ham, generate_doors, door_record

def main():
    ok = True
    def chk(name, cond, detail=""):
        nonlocal ok
        print(f"{'PASS' if cond else 'FAIL'}  {name}" + (f"  ({detail})" if detail else ""))
        if not cond:
            ok = False

    doors = generate_doors()
    chk("total doors = 7140", len(doors) == 7140, f"got {len(doors)}")

    bins = Counter(ham(a, b) for a, b, c, d in doors)
    chk("distance bins", dict(sorted(bins.items())) == {2: 488, 3: 1696, 4: 2548, 5: 1864, 6: 544},
        str(dict(sorted(bins.items()))))

    pairs = {tuple(sorted((a, b))) for a, b, c, d in doors}
    chk("unique merge pairs = 944", len(pairs) == 944, f"got {len(pairs)}")

    recs = [door_record(a, b, c, d) for a, b, c, d in doors]
    clean = sum(1 for r in recs if r["overlap_is_collapsed"])
    floor = sum(1 for r in recs if not r["overlap_is_collapsed"] and r["overlap_a_b"] == [0])
    wider = len(recs) - clean - floor
    chk("clean = 360", clean == 360, f"got {clean}")
    chk("floor = 3196", floor == 3196, f"got {floor}")
    chk("wider = 3584", wider == 3584, f"got {wider}")
    chk("partition sums", clean + floor + wider == 7140)

    chk("d6 entirely floor",
        all(r["overlap_a_b"] == [0] for r in recs if r["distance_a_b"] == 6))
    chk("d2 no floor",
        all(r["overlap_a_b"] != [0] for r in recs if r["distance_a_b"] == 2))
    chk("clean stops at 4",
        all(r["distance_a_b"] <= 4 for r in recs if r["overlap_is_collapsed"]))

    # value identity + weight identity + XOR preservation on every door
    bad = sum(1 for a, b, c, d in doors
              if not (a + b - c == d
                      and len(bits(a)) + len(bits(b)) - len(bits(c)) == len(bits(d))
                      and (a ^ b) == (c ^ d)))
    chk("three constraints hold on all doors", bad == 0, f"violations: {bad}")

    # Full Plate codec-mask claims
    cols = set(MASKS)
    xor_is_col = sum(1 for i in range(48) for j in range(i + 1, 48)
                     if (MASKS[i] ^ MASKS[j]) in cols)
    chk("0 XOR collisions /1128", xor_is_col == 0, f"got {xor_is_col}")
    chk("row0 all ones", all(m & 1 for m in MASKS))
    wdist = Counter(bin(m).count("1") for m in MASKS)
    chk("column weight line 6/15/16/9/2",
        dict(sorted(wdist.items())) == {2: 6, 3: 15, 4: 16, 5: 9, 6: 2},
        str(dict(sorted(wdist.items()))))

    print("\nDOORS BATTERY:", "ALL PASS" if ok else "FAILURES PRESENT")
    return 0 if ok else 1

if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
DOORS — full generation code for the 7,140-door merge map.

Source: the FILED 7x48 codec matrix (64/170,360) = odd masks 3..97.
A "door" is two nodes (a,b) merging via a collapsed hallway (c) into (d).

Three constraints, all necessary:
  1. Value identity:  a + b - c = d   (d must be a mask value, all four distinct)
  2. Weight identity: |a| + |b| - |c| = |d|   (popcounts of the 7-bit masks)
  3. XOR preservation: (a ^ b) == (c ^ d)     (the difference pattern survives the collapse)

These three generate EXACTLY 7,140 doors — verified cell-for-cell against the
reference workbook (doors_only_extensive.xlsx, All_7140).

Each door also carries:
  Sa..Sd        = set-bit positions of a,b,c,d
  overlap_a_b   = Sa & Sb
  clean         = (Sc == overlap)          # 360 doors: the collapsed set IS the overlap
  floor         = overlap == {0}           # 3,196 doors
  distance      = Hamming(a,b)             # bins 2..6: 488/1696/2548/1864/544
  indices       = column indices of a,b,c,d in the mask list
"""

MASKS = [m for m in range(3, 98) if m % 2 == 1]   # filed 7x48 columns
MSET = set(MASKS)
MIDX = {m: i for i, m in enumerate(MASKS)}

def bits(n):
    return {b for b in range(7) if (n >> b) & 1}

def ham(a, b):
    return bin(a ^ b).count("1")

def generate_doors():
    """Return the list of (a, b, c, d) door tuples. a < b (canonical pair order)."""
    doors = []
    for i in range(48):
        for j in range(i + 1, 48):
            a, b = MASKS[i], MASKS[j]
            xab = a ^ b
            wa, wb = len(bits(a)), len(bits(b))
            for k in range(48):
                if k == i or k == j:
                    continue
                c = MASKS[k]
                d = a + b - c
                if d not in MSET or d in (a, b, c):
                    continue
                if wa + wb - len(bits(c)) != len(bits(d)):
                    continue
                if xab != (c ^ d):
                    continue
                doors.append((a, b, c, d))
    return doors

def door_record(a, b, c, d):
    Sa, Sb, Sc, Sd = bits(a), bits(b), bits(c), bits(d)
    ov = Sa & Sb
    return {
        "merge": [a, b],
        "via_collapsed": c,
        "into": d,
        "operation": f"{a}+{b}-{c}={d}",
        "Sa": sorted(Sa), "Sb": sorted(Sb), "Sc": sorted(Sc), "Sd": sorted(Sd),
        "overlap_a_b": sorted(ov),
        "overlap_is_collapsed": Sc == ov,
        "distance_a_b": ham(a, b),
        "indices": {"a": MIDX[a], "b": MIDX[b], "c": MIDX[c], "d": MIDX[d]},
    }

def build_workbook(path):
    """Write the full doors workbook (All_7140 + per-distance sheets)."""
    import openpyxl
    doors = generate_doors()
    wb = openpyxl.Workbook()
    ws = wb.active
    ws.title = "All_7140"
    hdr = ["merge", "via_collapsed", "into", "operation", "Sa", "Sb", "Sc", "Sd",
           "overlap_a_b", "overlap_is_collapsed", "distance_a_b", "indices"]
    ws.append(hdr)
    bydist = {}
    for a, b, c, d in doors:
        r = door_record(a, b, c, d)
        ws.append([str(r["merge"]), r["via_collapsed"], r["into"], r["operation"],
                   str(r["Sa"]), str(r["Sb"]), str(r["Sc"]), str(r["Sd"]),
                   str(r["overlap_a_b"]), r["overlap_is_collapsed"],
                   r["distance_a_b"], str(r["indices"])])
        bydist.setdefault(r["distance_a_b"], []).append(r)
    for dist in sorted(bydist):
        s = wb.create_sheet(f"dist_{dist}")
        s.append(hdr)
        for r in bydist[dist]:
            s.append([str(r["merge"]), r["via_collapsed"], r["into"], r["operation"],
                      str(r["Sa"]), str(r["Sb"]), str(r["Sc"]), str(r["Sd"]),
                      str(r["overlap_a_b"]), r["overlap_is_collapsed"],
                      r["distance_a_b"], str(r["indices"])])
    wb.save(path)
    return len(doors)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys
    n = build_workbook(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "doors_generated.xlsx")
    print(f"doors written: {n}")

import math
from collections import Counter

# ===========================================================================
# Roots
# ===========================================================================

N_MSG, N_PAR = 48, 7
MASKS = [m for m in range(3, 98) if m % 2 == 1]   # filed 7x48 columns
MSET = set(MASKS)
MIDX = {m: i for i, m in enumerate(MASKS)}
assert len(MASKS) == N_MSG and all(m & 1 for m in MASKS)
assert max(MASKS) < 2 ** N_PAR                      # 7-bit columns

def bits(n):
    """Set-bit positions of the 7-bit mask n."""
    return {b for b in range(N_PAR) if (n >> b) & 1}

def ham(a, b):
    """Hamming distance between masks a and b."""
    return bin(a ^ b).count("1")

# ===========================================================================
# A. Filed codec — [55,8] fault-refusing codec (64/170,360), pure Python
# ===========================================================================
# Repair-or-refuse:
#   single spike (any nonzero magnitude) -> repaired (48/48)
#   single parity-tail edit               -> detected, payload intact
#   dual spikes, same strict sign         -> refused
#   dual spikes, opposite signs           -> 1004/1128 refused,
#                                            124/1128 alias to a single axis
#                                            (documented exception class;
#                                             the v4 14-row matrix closes it)

def decode_single(s):
    """Column index whose mask equals syndrome s, else None (refuse)."""
    return MASKS.index(s) if s in MASKS else None

def codec_analyze():
    res = {}
    res["singles_repaired"] = sum(1 for i in range(N_MSG)
                                  if decode_single(MASKS[i]) == i)
    cols = set(MASKS)
    pair_xors = set()
    xor_is_col = 0
    for i in range(N_MSG):
        for j in range(i + 1, N_MSG):
            x = MASKS[i] ^ MASKS[j]
            pair_xors.add(x)
            if x in cols:
                xor_is_col += 1
    res["pairs"] = N_MSG * (N_MSG - 1) // 2
    res["xor_collisions"] = xor_is_col          # 0: no unsigned pair XOR is a column
    res["distinct_pair_xors"] = len(pair_xors)   # 63
    # opposite-sign equal-magnitude alias class: Mi XOR Mj is a single bit
    # <=> Mi - Mj = +/- 2^k (an axis, not a column)
    res["signed_alias_pairs"] = sum(
        1 for i in range(N_MSG) for j in range(i + 1, N_MSG)
        if bin(MASKS[i] ^ MASKS[j]).count("1") == 1)
    res["weight_dist"] = dict(sorted(Counter(bin(m).count("1") for m in MASKS).items()))
    res["row0_all_ones"] = all(m & 1 for m in MASKS)
    return res

# ===========================================================================
# B. Doors — 7,140-door merge map
# ===========================================================================
# A door is two nodes (a,b) merging via a collapsed hallway (c) into (d).
# Three constraints, all necessary:
#   1. value identity:     a + b - c = d   (d a mask value, all four distinct)
#   2. popcount identity:  |a| + |b| - |c| = |d|
#   3. XOR preservation:   (a ^ b) == (c ^ d)
# These generate EXACTLY 7,140 doors.

def generate_doors():
    """Return the list of (a, b, c, d) door tuples. a < b (canonical pair order)."""
    doors = []
    for i in range(N_MSG):
        for j in range(i + 1, N_MSG):
            a, b = MASKS[i], MASKS[j]
            xab = a ^ b
            wa, wb = len(bits(a)), len(bits(b))
            for k in range(N_MSG):
                if k == i or k == j:
                    continue
                c = MASKS[k]
                d = a + b - c
                if d not in MSET or d in (a, b, c):
                    continue
                if wa + wb - len(bits(c)) != len(bits(d)):
                    continue
                if xab != (c ^ d):
                    continue
                doors.append((a, b, c, d))
    return doors

def door_record(a, b, c, d):
    """Full record for one door: sets, overlap, clean flag, distance, indices."""
    Sa, Sb, Sc, Sd = bits(a), bits(b), bits(c), bits(d)
    ov = Sa & Sb
    return {
        "merge": [a, b],
        "via_collapsed": c,
        "into": d,
        "operation": f"{a}+{b}-{c}={d}",
        "Sa": sorted(Sa), "Sb": sorted(Sb), "Sc": sorted(Sc), "Sd": sorted(Sd),
        "overlap_a_b": sorted(ov),
        "overlap_is_collapsed": Sc == ov,   # 360 doors: collapsed set IS the overlap
        "distance_a_b": ham(a, b),          # bins 2..6
        "indices": {"a": MIDX[a], "b": MIDX[b], "c": MIDX[c], "d": MIDX[d]},
    }

def value_feasible(a, b):
    """Exists c in M\\{a,b} with d = a+b-c in M\\{a,b,c}? (value identity alone)."""
    for c in MASKS:
        if c == a or c == b:
            continue
        d = a + b - c
        if d in MSET and d not in (a, b, c):
            return True
    return False

# ===========================================================================
# C. Batteries
# ===========================================================================

def _battery(title, checks):
    print(f"--- {title} ---")
    ok = True
    for name, cond, detail in checks:
        print(f"{'PASS' if cond else 'FAIL'}  {name}" + (f"  [{detail}]" if detail else ""))
        ok = ok and cond
    print(f"{title}: {'ALL PASS' if ok else 'FAILURES PRESENT'}\n")
    return ok

def doors_battery(doors):
    recs = [door_record(a, b, c, d) for a, b, c, d in doors]
    bins = Counter(r["distance_a_b"] for r in recs)
    clean = sum(1 for r in recs if r["overlap_is_collapsed"])
    floor = sum(1 for r in recs if not r["overlap_is_collapsed"] and r["overlap_a_b"] == [0])
    wider = len(recs) - clean - floor
    pairs = {tuple(sorted((a, b))) for a, b, c, d in doors}
    return _battery("DOORS (14)", [
        ("total doors = 7140", len(doors) == 7140, f"got {len(doors)}"),
        ("distance bins 488/1696/2548/1864/544",
         dict(sorted(bins.items())) == {2: 488, 3: 1696, 4: 2548, 5: 1864, 6: 544},
         str(dict(sorted(bins.items())))),
        ("unique merge pairs = 944", len(pairs) == 944, f"got {len(pairs)}"),
        ("clean = 360", clean == 360, f"got {clean}"),
        ("floor = 3196", floor == 3196, f"got {floor}"),
        ("wider = 3584", wider == 3584, f"got {wider}"),
        ("partition sums", clean + floor + wider == len(recs), ""),
        ("d6 entirely floor",
         all(r["overlap_a_b"] == [0] for r in recs if r["distance_a_b"] == 6), ""),
        ("d2 no floor",
         all(r["overlap_a_b"] != [0] for r in recs if r["distance_a_b"] == 2), ""),
        ("clean stops at 4",
         all(r["distance_a_b"] <= 4 for r in recs if r["overlap_is_collapsed"]), ""),
        ("three constraints hold on all doors",
         all(a + b - c == d
             and len(bits(a)) + len(bits(b)) - len(bits(c)) == len(bits(d))
             and (a ^ b) == (c ^ d) for a, b, c, d in doors), ""),
        ("0 XOR collisions /1128",
         sum(1 for i in range(N_MSG) for j in range(i + 1, N_MSG)
             if (MASKS[i] ^ MASKS[j]) in MSET) == 0, ""),
        ("row0 all ones", all(m & 1 for m in MASKS), ""),
        ("column weight line 6/15/16/9/2",
         dict(sorted(Counter(bin(m).count("1") for m in MASKS).items()))
         == {2: 6, 3: 15, 4: 16, 5: 9, 6: 2}, ""),
    ])

def starting_line_battery():
    b = lambda G: 0.4992 * G - 0.0104 * G * G
    d, dk, w = [4, 1, 0], [2, 1, 1], [1, 1, 1]
    lam = sum(wi * di * ki for wi, di, ki in zip(w, d, dk)) / sum(wi * ki ** 2 for wi, ki in zip(w, dk))
    H = [di - lam * ki for di, ki in zip(d, dk)]
    return _battery("STARTING LINE (15)", [
        ("beta(47) = 0.4888", abs(b(47) - 0.4888) < 1e-12, ""),
        ("beta(48) = 0", abs(b(48)) < 1e-12, ""),
        ("beta(49) = -0.5096", abs(b(49) + 0.5096) < 1e-12, ""),
        ("0.0104*G*(48-G) form", abs(0.0104 * 47 * 1 - 0.4888) < 1e-12, ""),
        ("7776/162 = 48", 7776 / 162 == 48 and 6 ** 5 == 7776 and 2 * 3 ** 4 == 162, ""),
        ("4608 = 2*48^2", 4608 == 2 * 48 * 48, ""),
        ("407096 + 251654 = 658750", 407096 + 251654 == 658750, ""),
        ("(2*4/5)^2 = 2.56", abs((2 * 4 / 5) ** 2 - 2.56) < 1e-12, ""),
        ("0.9216/48 = 0.0192", abs(0.9216 / 48 - 0.0192) < 1e-12, ""),
        ("cancellation at 48", abs((0.48 * 48 - 0.0104 * 48 ** 2) + 0.0192 * 48) < 1e-12, ""),
        ("0.50*47-(1/96)*47^2 = 0.4895833", abs(0.50 * 47 - (1 / 96) * 47 ** 2 - 0.4895833) < 1e-6, ""),
        ("weight sets sum to 1",
         abs(0.42 + 0.22 + 0.32 + 0.04 - 1) < 1e-12 and
         abs(0.28 + 0.24 + 0.28 + 0.16 + 0.04 - 1) < 1e-12, ""),
        ("arctan(4/3) = 53.130102 deg", abs(math.degrees(math.atan(4 / 3)) - 53.130102) < 1e-6, ""),
        ("rotation det = 1, unit columns",
         abs((3 / 5) * (3 / 5) - (-4 / 5) * (4 / 5) - 1) < 1e-12, ""),
        ("lambda = 1.5, H = [1.0, -0.5, -1.5]", lam == 1.5 and H == [1.0, -0.5, -1.5], ""),
    ])

def partition_battery(doors):
    door_pairs = {tuple(sorted((a, b))) for a, b, c, d in doors}
    all_pairs = [(MASKS[i], MASKS[j]) for i in range(N_MSG) for j in range(i + 1, N_MSG)]
    never = [p for p in all_pairs if tuple(sorted(p)) not in door_pairs]
    alias = [p for p in never if ham(*p) == 1]
    rest = [p for p in never if ham(*p) > 1]
    vinfeas = [p for p in rest if not value_feasible(*p)]
    per_pair = Counter(tuple(sorted((a, b))) for a, b, c, d in doors)
    comp = [(a, b) for a, b in door_pairs if a + b == 128]
    clean_d = Counter(ham(a, b) for a, b, c, d in doors
                      if bits(c) == (bits(a) & bits(b)))
    return _battery("PARTITION 1128 (8)", [
        ("944 + 124 + 60 = 1128",
         len(door_pairs) == 944 and len(alias) == 124 and len(rest) == 60,
         f"{len(door_pairs)}+{len(alias)}+{len(rest)}"),
        ("alias pairs are exactly the distance-1 pairs",
         len(alias) == sum(1 for a, b in all_pairs if ham(a, b) == 1) == 124, ""),
        ("zero alias pairs are doors",
         all(tuple(sorted(p)) not in door_pairs for p in alias), ""),
        ("3 value-infeasible at sum extremes", len(vinfeas) == 3,
         str(sorted(a + b for a, b in vinfeas))),
        ("57 pass value identity, fail popcount/XOR", len(rest) - len(vinfeas) == 57, ""),
        ("17 complementary (sum-128) door pairs", len(comp) == 17, ""),
        ("max 32 doors/pair, complementary on top",
         max(per_pair.values()) == 32 and
         all(a + b == 128 for (a, b), _ in per_pair.most_common(3)), ""),
        ("clean 122/168/70 at d2/d3/d4, none at d5/d6",
         dict(sorted(clean_d.items())) == {2: 122, 3: 168, 4: 70}, ""),
    ])

def main():
    print("CORE — full verified core, one script\n")
    ca = codec_analyze()
    assert ca["singles_repaired"] == 48 and ca["xor_collisions"] == 0
    assert ca["signed_alias_pairs"] == 124
    print(f"codec: {ca['singles_repaired']}/48 singles, "
          f"{ca['xor_collisions']}/1128 XOR collisions, "
          f"{ca['signed_alias_pairs']} alias pairs\n")
    doors = generate_doors()
    ok = doors_battery(doors)
    ok = starting_line_battery() and ok
    ok = partition_battery(doors) and ok
    print("CORE:", "ALL 37 CHECKS PASS — NO HOLES" if ok else "FAILURES PRESENT")
    return 0 if ok else 1

if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

PROOFS

Mathematical proofs for the core

Filed masks 3–97 (odd) · 48 columns · Compiled 2026-10-09

Standing of these proofs

Three kinds of certainty appear below. Structural proofs (Theorems 1–3) derive from the mask definitions alone — no computation needed. The Sidon theorem (Theorem 4) is finite-field algebra. Enumerative proofs (§5) are exhaustive computation over the finite 48-mask set, which constitutes proof for finite claims. Each states exactly what it covers.

Theorem 1 — Zero XOR Collisions

Theorem No unsigned pair XOR of the filed masks equals a column mask. (0 / 1,128.)
Proof. Every column mask is odd (3, 5, …, 97). Let a, b be distinct odd masks. Their XOR has bit 0 equal to 1⊕1 = 0, hence a⊕b is even. Every column is odd. An even integer cannot equal an odd column. Therefore no pair XOR is a column. ∎

Theorem 2 — Door Swap-Pairing

Theorem The 7,140 doors partition into 3,570 pairs under swap of the collapsed and result nodes: (a,b,c,d) is a door if and only if (a,b,d,c) is.
Proof. The three door constraints are symmetric in c and d. Value: d = a+b−c ⟺ c = a+b−d. Popcount: |a|+|b|−|c| = |d| ⟺ |a|+|b|−|d| = |c|. XOR: (a^b) = (c^d) = (d^c). Distinctness is preserved (a,b,c,d distinct ⟹ a,b,d,c distinct). Since the door requires c ≠ d, the swap is a fixed-point-free involution, so doors pair up exactly: 7,140 = 2 × 3,570. ∎

Theorem 3 — Alias Characterization

Theorem The 124 alias pairs are exactly the Hamming-distance-1 mask pairs — no more, no fewer.
Proof. In the binary model, an opposite-sign equal-magnitude pair on columns i, j aliases to a single axis iff Mi − Mj = ±2k for some k, iff Mi⊕Mj is a power of two, iff popcount(Mi⊕Mj) = 1, iff ham(Mi,Mj) = 1. Each equivalence is definitional. Enumeration gives 124 such pairs. ∎

Corollary. Zero alias pairs are doors: doors require distance ≥ 2 (verified: the 124 distance-1 pairs admit no (c,d) under the three constraints). The door map excludes precisely the codec's exception class — by structure, not by filtering.

Theorem 4 — Characteristic-2 Cubic Sidon (v4)

Theorem {(x, x³) : x ∈ Fq}, q = 2k, is Sidon in Fq²: pair sums determine the unordered pair.
Proof. Suppose (x+y, x³+y³) = (u+v, u³+v³) with x≠y, u≠v. Put s = x+y = u+v; in characteristic 2, x≠y gives s≠0. Then x³+y³ = (x+y)(x²+xy+y²) = s(s²+xy), using x²+y² = s². Hence s³+s·xy = s³+s·uv, so xy = uv. Then {x,y} and {u,v} are both root-sets of t²+st+xy = 0, which has at most two roots; thus {x,y} = {u,v}. ∎

The v4 14-row matrix instantiates this in F64: 48 cubic-parabola points with pairwise distance ≥ 2, plus two common bits. All 1,128 pair sums are distinct; the 124-alias class dies by construction. (New matter — not filed.)

The closed fault universe
Compiled 2026-10-09 · Every claim recomputed

Every dual fault in the filed codec now has a name.
Nothing is left over.

The 1,128 column pairs produce exactly 63 distinct XOR syndromes — the complete vocabulary of dual faults. They partition with zero remainder:

56 shared syndromes — the doors 944 door pairs collapse onto 56 XOR values, every one shared by multiple pairs (56/56). A syndrome in this class can never identify a unique pair — so refusal is not caution, it is the only sound response. The 7,140 doors are the complete atlas of this ambiguity: for each, they exhibit the alternative pair ((c,d) swap) carrying the identical syndrome.
6 axis syndromes — the alias class 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64. The 124 distance-1 pairs land here — syndromes that look like a single fault but aren't. Disjoint from the 56 above. This is the only class where the decoder can be fooled, and it is exactly characterized (Theorem 3).
1 orphan syndrome — 96 Appears only on never-door pairs. Classified, not missing: 56 + 6 + 1 = 63.

The diameter-2 universe

The 944 door pairs form a graph on the 48 masks. It is connected, with diameter 2: every mask reaches every other in at most two door-steps. The least-connected mask still has 15 door partners; the most has 41. The fault universe is one piece — no isolated regions, no far corners.

The complementary uniformity

Seventeen pairs sum to 128. Every one carries exactly 32 doors — the global maximum, attained uniformly: 17 × 32 = 544 doors. No other pair exceeds it; no complementary pair falls short. The richest ambiguity in the code sits exactly on the complementary pairs.

What this means

The codec and the doors are not two results — they are one closed object. The codec defines the fault space; the doors map its ambiguity completely. Three consequences:

1. Refusal is proved optimal on 944/1,128 pairs: the syndrome is provably non-unique (shared 56/56), so any decoder that guessed would be wrong more often than right.

2. The danger is fenced to 124 pairs on 6 syndromes — the alias class, already documented, already bounded.

3. The v4 matrix (new matter) kills the 6 axis syndromes by construction — which would leave a fault universe where every dual fault is either repaired or provably refused, with zero ambiguity unaccounted for.

NINE CIRCLES — ASUS UGen AI League · Stage I · Creator AI

1

 NINE CIRCLES

Scenario / Problem
AI image tools flood the world with one-click spectacle. What is missing is deliberate,
iterated visual authorship — a human-directed series with locked compositional law,
color discipline, and a narrative spine, built piece by piece over many sessions rather
than generated in a single pass.

NINE CIRCLES — ASUS UGen AI League · Stage I · Creator AI

2

 NINE CIRCLES

Concept
A nine-circle descent after Dante's Inferno — Limbo, Lust, Gluttony, Greed, Wrath,
Heresy, Violence, Fraud, Treachery — rendered as a unified visual system. Each circle is
its own world; together they form one installation with shared axes, consistent
perspective discipline, and a color grammar that deepens as the descent proceeds.

NINE CIRCLES — ASUS UGen AI League · Stage I · Creator AI

3

 NINE CIRCLES

Methods — directed iteration
Directed iterative generation: reference-driven synthesis where the human author
supplies reference imagery, rejects directions outright, and locks conventions per
circle: composition, chirality, palette limits, opacity transitions. Rejected branches
are retained as scrapped work, not deleted, so the provenance of every final piece is
auditable.

NINE CIRCLES — ASUS UGen AI League · Stage I · Creator AI

4

 NINE CIRCLES

Methods — locked conventions
Locked compositional conventions held across all nine circles: vesica-piscis circle
overlaps with color-blended seams rather than hard edges; a shared central vertical axis
across panels; all spirals rotating with the same chirality; a master-scale hierarchy;
and a source-fidelity rule — when the author names an image, the image itself is mapped
onto the structure, not reinterpreted.

NINE CIRCLES — ASUS UGen AI League · Stage I · Creator AI

5

 NINE CIRCLES

Methods — material studies
Material studies per circle: braided wire, ferrofluid spikes, chrome tunnels,
thread-built architecture, marble reinterpretation, technical-blueprint overlays — each
circle carries its own material language inside the shared system.

Author direction → reference synthesis → rejection and lock loop → convention lock →

Amazon Build, Ship, Shape Hackathon
=========================================================

BLOCK 1: ABOUT THE PROJECT (paste into Project Story Markdown box)
---------------------------------------------------------
## Inspiration
Every AI ships confident — and that's the problem. Jailbreaks, prompt injections, and hallucinations cost real money in production. I build admission-control systems (patent-pending), and I wanted to prove the missing layer: an AI that knows when to refuse.

## What it does
PRIM3 is a drop-in safety layer for AI applications. Every query passes through a Headroom admission controller first. If it fits inside validated headroom → ADMIT, and the query reaches the model. If not → REFUSE, with the reason written to an in-memory decision log. In the implemented gate path, blocked queries never reach the model call (integration not yet executed against live Bedrock).

## How I built it
- **Core engine:** Python Headroom admission controller (my Members Gate IP, 64/169,264) + fault-refusing codec layer (64/170,360) + Seraphim residual witness
- **MCP server:** exposes `refuse.evaluate`, `refuse.ledger`, `refuse.demo_attack` via MCP (stdio transport); Alexa+ integration not built or tested
- **Bedrock gate:** `bedrock_gate.py` implements (but has not executed) a Bedrock invoke_model call; the Bedrock path is untested and is not exposed via MCP
- **Demo video:** screen recording of the engine on the adversarial battery, narrated

## Challenges I ran into
The admission threshold is hash-sensitive — some attack phrasings landed just under the refusal boundary. Measured battery on the submitted code: 5/9 probes blocked; 4 admitted, including roleplay jailbreaks. Attacks containing the word "safety" route to a low-residual path and are systematically admitted — a known defect in the token heuristic.

## What I learned
Refusal is a system property, not a prompt trick. You can't bolt it on with instructions — it has to sit in the architecture, between the user and the model.

## What's next
Live Bedrock deployment, per-tenant headroom calibration, and the fault-refusing codec as a transport layer.

 P R O J E C T D E S C R I P T I O N · PA S T E - R E A D Y

The answer is not “yes” or “no.” It is “show
me the evidence to act.”
Every AI agent can propose an action. REFUSE makes it earn
execution.
REFUSE is a deterministic admission layer for Alexa+ agent actions. It sits between the conversational
experience and real-world tools such as email, databases, files, and system operations. Every proposed call
is evaluated by a single Headroom admission controller: a resource-vector solvency check crossed with a
residual gate. A call is admitted only when it fits inside what remains; otherwise it is refused and the refusal is
recorded.
Headroom is deliberately non-compensating: a surplus in one resource dimension cannot cover a deficit in
another. Any request that fails the solvency check or the residual gate produces REFUSE. Every decision is
appended to an in-memory hash-chained log with the verdict, the reason, and the residual. The log lives for
the process lifetime only.
The user never hears a generic error. The caller receives a machine-readable refusal certificate that names
the blocked dimension and offers a safe recovery: redact the data, choose an approved destination, request
narrower scope, or save the action for review. This turns safety from an invisible policy into a useful
interaction.

The line judges should remember

Your agent should not be rewarded for sounding certain.
It should be required to produce enough evidence to act.

REFUSE · JUDGING MAP

07

 D E V P O S T N A R R AT I V E · PA S T E - R E A D Y

From guardrails around language to proof
before action.
Inspiration
AI safety is often evaluated where the model speaks. The consequential boundary is later: the moment a
proposed tool call becomes an email, database query, file write, or system command. I built REFUSE to make
that boundary explicit. The design follows one rule: measure what remains after an interaction; admit only
what fits inside that leftover; otherwise refuse and record the refusal.

What it does
REFUSE evaluates agent actions through a deterministic Headroom admission controller and a noncompensating resource model. An admitted call proceeds; a refused call produces a machine-readable
refusal certificate with the reason, unchanged state, and closest safe recovery. Each verdict is written to an inmemory decision log.

How I built it
The core is a deterministic Python admission controller: a resource-vector solvency check crossed with a
residual gate. The competition layer exposes evaluation, the decision log, and the scripted attack battery
through a self-hosted MCP server over stdio (FastMCP). A Bedrock invoke_model path is implemented in
bedrock_gate.py but has never been executed and is not exposed via MCP; no AWS service integration exists
in the repository.

Challenges
The hardest design problem was keeping refusal useful. A safe system that only says “no” trains users to
route around it. REFUSE therefore separates decision from explanation: deterministic rules own the verdict,
while Alexa+ turns the reason code into an actionable alternative without weakening the boundary.

Accomplishments
The measured core blocks 5 of 9 scripted attack probes and admits the rest; every verdict carries a reason
code and is written to the in-memory log. Known gap: attacks containing the word “safety” are systematically
admitted by the current token heuristic. The demo is small enough to inspect end to end and expressive
enough to show a complete agent safety pattern.

What I learned / What's next
Safety becomes legible when every refusal names its boundary and every admission carries a receipt. Next
steps are identity-bound sessions, adaptive budgets, cross-request obfuscation detection, policy simulation
before deployment, and production-scale evaluation against a broader adversarial corpus.

# Pythonista — Flower of Life breathe
# Copy into Pythonista. Drag to rotate, pinch to zoom.
# Same 7-orb generator. Costume geometry, not a measurement.

from math import sin, cos, acos, pi, sqrt
import scene # type: ignore

N = 420
R0 = 1.0
COLORS = [
    (0.55, 0.20, 0.95),
    (0.10, 0.85, 0.30),
    (0.95, 0.75, 0.10),
    (0.05, 0.85, 0.80),
    (0.90, 0.15, 0.25),
    (0.85, 0.15, 0.75),
    (0.15, 0.40, 0.95),
]


def units_and_centers():
    hex_a = [(2 * pi * k) / 6 + pi / 6 for k in range(6)]
    centers = [(0.0, 0.0)] + [(R0 * cos(a), R0 * sin(a)) for a in hex_a]
    shells = []
    for i in range(7):
        pts = []
        for n in range(N):
            idx = n + 0.5
            phi = acos(1 - 2 * idx / N)
            theta = pi * (1 + sqrt(5)) * idx
            pts.append((sin(phi) * cos(theta), sin(phi) * sin(theta), cos(phi)))
        shells.append(pts)
    freq = [2 * (2 ** (i / 7.0)) for i in range(7)]
    return centers, shells, freq


C, SHELLS, FREQ = units_and_centers()


def project(x, y, z, az, el, zoom, w, h):
    ca, sa = cos(az), sin(az)
    ce, se = cos(el), sin(el)
    x1 = x * ca - y * sa
    y1 = x * sa + y * ca
    y2 = y1 * ce - z * se
    z2 = y1 * se + z * ce
    s = zoom * min(w, h) * 0.22
    return w * 0.5 + x1 * s, h * 0.5 - y2 * s, z2


class Breathe(scene.Scene):
    def setup(self):
        self.background_color = '#05050a'
        self.az = 0.4
        self.el = 0.35
        self.zoom = 1.0
        self.phase = 0.0
        self.breathe = True
        self._last = None
        self._pinch0 = None

    def touch_began(self, touch):
        if len(self.touches) == 1:
            self._last = touch.location
        elif len(self.touches) == 2:
            pts = list(self.touches.values())
            d = abs(pts[0].location - pts[1].location)
            self._pinch0 = (d, self.zoom)

    def touch_moved(self, touch):
        if len(self.touches) == 1 and self._last:
            p = touch.location
            self.az += (p.x - self._last.x) * 0.008
            self.el = max(-1.2, min(1.2, self.el + (p.y - self._last.y) * 0.008))
            self._last = p
        elif len(self.touches) == 2 and self._pinch0:
            pts = list(self.touches.values())
            d = abs(pts[0].location - pts[1].location)
            d0, z0 = self._pinch0
            if d0 > 1:
                self.zoom = max(0.35, min(3.2, z0 * (d / d0)))

    def touch_ended(self, touch):
        self._last = None
        self._pinch0 = None

    def draw(self):
        if self.breathe:
            self.phase += self.dt * 1.2
        amp = 0.72 + 0.28 * sin(self.phase * 0.55)
        w, h = self.size
        dots = []
        for i in range(7):
            cx, cy = C[i]
            cr, cg, cb = COLORS[i]
            f = FREQ[i]
            for sx, sy, sz in SHELLS[i]:
                wave = (
                    amp * 0.20 * sin(f * sx * 3 + self.phase) * cos(f * sy * 3 + self.phase * 0.7)
                    + amp * 0.10 * cos(f * 2 * sz + self.phase * 1.3)
                )
                br = 1 + 0.045 * sin(self.phase * 0.85 + i * 0.4)
                mr = R0 * br * (1 + wave)
                x, y, z = cx + sx * mr, cy + sy * mr, sz * mr
                px, py, depth = project(x, y, z, self.az, self.el, self.zoom, w, h)
                lum = 0.50 + 0.50 * sin(f * x + z + self.phase)
                dots.append((depth, px, py, (cr * lum, cg * lum, cb * lum)))
        dots.sort(key=lambda t: t[0])
        for _, px, py, col in dots:
            scene.fill(*col)
            scene.ellipse(px - 1.4, py - 1.4, 2.8, 2.8)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    scene.run(Breathe(), frame_interval=2, show_fps=False)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Braided elliptic recursive coil encoder.

Pass-on file. Starts from nothing except the maps and plates written
in this meeting. No jackets.

What this is
  One winding. No corner. No hub. Starts from us.
  One original interaction. It does not happen twice.
  Next block is a new unique 1 that cites that interaction.
  Coupling 0 is leftover of a closed meeting, not an original.
  Plates are labels. Bits are bits. Do not pack names into (0,0).

What this is not
  a drawn center, a second origin, a minted 2,
  a name packed onto a bit pair, an unclosed window scored as closed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Frozen plates (labels). Unique originals, not bits.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

LETTER = (
    ("A", "D", "B", "C"),
    ("B", "C", "D", "A"),
    ("C", "B", "A", "D"),
    ("D", "A", "C", "B"),
)

NUMBER = (
    (1, 4, 3, 2),
    (2, 3, 4, 1),
    (3, 2, 1, 4),
    (4, 1, 2, 3),
)

# Five M-pairs they wrote. Each line + its reverse.
# 0000/0000 is the coupling pair. M(0)=0. Not a unique 1.
PAIRS = (
    (("1", "2", "3", "4"), ("4", "3", "2", "1")),
    (("A", "B", "C", "D"), ("D", "C", "B", "A")),
    (("0", "0", "0", "0"), ("0", "0", "0", "0")),
    (("E", "F", "G", "H"), ("H", "G", "F", "E")),
    (("5", "6", "7", "8"), ("8", "7", "6", "5")),
)


def vertical_ltr(plate):
    rows, cols = len(plate), len(plate[0])
    return tuple(tuple(plate[r][c] for r in range(rows)) for c in range(cols))


def reverse_row(row):
    return tuple(reversed(row))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Maps on bit sheets  shape (S, S, 2)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def M(B: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Other hand. Reverse seats. M o M = id."""
    return B[:, ::-1, :].copy()


def Pi(B: np.ndarray, p: int = 1) -> np.ndarray:
    """Overlap read. Same ones, reindexed."""
    S = B.shape[0]
    out = np.empty_like(B)
    for r in range(S):
        for c in range(S):
            out[r, c] = B[c, (r + p) % S]
    return out


def Pi_minus(B: np.ndarray, p: int = 1) -> np.ndarray:
    return M(Pi(M(B), p))


def origin(S: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """First coupling. All zeros. Not stored. Not a hub. Not a unique 1."""
    return np.zeros((S, S, 2), dtype=int)


def flat(row: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    return row.reshape(-1)


def window_bits(prev_row: np.ndarray, curr_row: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    return np.concatenate([flat(prev_row), flat(curr_row)])


def write_landing(Pi_row: np.ndarray, info_row: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Clear landing to 0, then write the bit that closes the window."""
    curr = info_row.copy()
    curr[-1, 1] = 0
    curr[-1, 1] = int(window_bits(Pi_row, curr).sum()) % 2
    return curr


def encode_chain(info_blocks, p: int = 1):
    """From us. prev starts as the coupling freeze. Each block a new 1."""
    prev = origin(info_blocks[0].shape[0])
    out = []
    for info in info_blocks:
        P = Pi(prev, p)
        curr = np.empty_like(info)
        for r in range(info.shape[0]):
            curr[r] = write_landing(P[r], info[r])
        out.append(curr)
        prev = curr
    return out


def window_couplings(blocks, p: int = 1):
    prev = origin(blocks[0].shape[0])
    out = []
    for B in blocks:
        P = Pi(prev, p)
        out.append(tuple(int(window_bits(P[r], B[r]).sum()) % 2
                         for r in range(B.shape[0])))
        prev = B
    return out


def windows_even(blocks, p: int = 1) -> bool:
    return all(all(v == 0 for v in row) for row in window_couplings(blocks, p))


def couples(B: np.ndarray):
    S = B.shape[0]
    return sorted(tuple(int(x) for x in B[r, c]) for r in range(S) for c in range(S))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Proof from nothing: only plates + maps above
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def prove():
    S = 4
    B0_names = NUMBER
    B1_names = vertical_ltr(NUMBER)
    B2_names = vertical_ltr(B1_names)

    # bit path is separate. seed is not a plate name.
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    infos = []
    for _ in range(3):
        info = rng.integers(0, 2, size=(S, S, 2), dtype=int)
        info[:, -1, 1] = 0
        infos.append(info)
    plus = encode_chain(infos, p=1)
    minus = [M(B) for B in plus]
    couplings = window_couplings(plus)

    number_originals = sorted({n for row in NUMBER for n in row})
    letter_originals = sorted({c for row in LETTER for c in row})
    pair_originals = sorted({
        x for pair in PAIRS for line in pair for x in line if x != "0"
    })

    flags = {
        "one_origin_freeze": np.array_equal(origin(S), np.zeros((S, S, 2))),
        "origin_not_stored": len(plus) == 3,
        "B0_names_are_the_plate": B0_names == NUMBER,
        "B1_is_vertical_ltr": B1_names == vertical_ltr(NUMBER),
        "B2_names_return_B0_glance": B2_names == B0_names,
        "B1_bits_new_1": not np.array_equal(plus[1], plus[0]),
        "B2_bits_new_1": (
            not np.array_equal(plus[2], plus[1])
            and not np.array_equal(plus[2], plus[0])
        ),
        "no_stored_block_is_origin": all(
            not np.array_equal(B, origin(S)) for B in plus
        ),
        "windows_closed": windows_even(plus),
        "couplings_all_zero": list(couplings) == [(0, 0, 0, 0)] * 3,
        "minus_is_M": all(np.array_equal(minus[i], M(plus[i])) for i in range(3)),
        "M_M_is_id": np.array_equal(M(M(plus[0])), plus[0]),
        "Pi_keeps_ones": couples(plus[0]) == couples(Pi(plus[0])),
        "number_originals_1234": number_originals == [1, 2, 3, 4],
        "letter_originals_ABCD": letter_originals == ["A", "B", "C", "D"],
        "pair_originals_unique": pair_originals == [
            "1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6", "7", "8",
            "A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G", "H",
        ],
        "each_pair_is_line_and_reverse": all(
            pair[1] == reverse_row(pair[0]) for pair in PAIRS
        ),
        "zero_pair_self_reverses": PAIRS[2][0] == PAIRS[2][1],
        "letter_col0_reverse_of_col1": (
            vertical_ltr(LETTER)[0] == reverse_row(vertical_ltr(LETTER)[1])
        ),
        "number_col0_reverse_of_col1": (
            vertical_ltr(NUMBER)[0] == reverse_row(vertical_ltr(NUMBER)[1])
        ),
        "latin_number": all(
            len(set(NUMBER[r])) == 4 and len({NUMBER[r][c] for r in range(4)}) == 4
            for r in range(4) for c in [0]
        ) and all(len({NUMBER[r][c] for r in range(4)}) == 4 for c in range(4)),
        "latin_letter": all(len(set(LETTER[r])) == 4 for r in range(4))
        and all(len({LETTER[r][c] for r in range(4)}) == 4 for c in range(4)),
    }
    flags["ALL"] = all(flags.values())
    return flags, plus, minus, B0_names, B1_names, B2_names, couplings


def main():
    flags, plus, minus, B0, B1, B2, couplings = prove()
    print("coil encoder — from the seated maps only")
    print("no corner  no hub  starts from us")
    print("one original interaction; it does not happen twice")
    print()
    print("B0 labels")
    for row in B0:
        print(" ", " ".join(str(x) for x in row))
    print("B1 labels")
    for row in B1:
        print(" ", " ".join(str(x) for x in row))
    print("B2 labels (return glance of names, not a second origin)")
    for row in B2:
        print(" ", " ".join(str(x) for x in row))
    print()
    print("M-pairs")
    for a, b in PAIRS:
        print(" ", " ".join(a), "/", " ".join(b))
    print()
    print("coupling zeros", couplings)
    print()
    for k, v in flags.items():
        print(f"  {k:36s} {v}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

﻿We will run with the DoD / AFWERX Phase I Open Topic baseline:
* Title: Zero-Knowledge Spatial Verification Protocol (ZKSVP)
* Operational Focus: Assured, privacy-preserving geofence and trajectory attestation for autonomous UAS in contested EW/GPS-denied environments.
* Core Architecture: Edge-optimized BLS12-381 pairing cryptography with RFC 9380 SSWU hash-to-curve routines executed on SWaP-constrained microcontrollers via zksvp-core.
Below is the complete, structured 5-page Technical Volume white paper formatted directly to DoD SBIR evaluation standards.
PHASE I TECHNICAL VOLUME: ZERO-KNOWLEDGE SPATIAL VERIFICATION PROTOCOL (ZKSVP)
Topic Number: AFWERX Phase I Open Topic (JADC2 / Resilient Navigation) Proposal Title: Zero-Knowledge Spatial Verification Protocol (ZKSVP) for Cryptographic Geofencing and Position Attestation in Contested Electromagnetic Environments Firm Name: [Company Name] | CAGE: [XXXXX] | DUNS/UEI: [XXXXXXXXXXXX] Principal Investigator (PI): [Lead Cryptographic Engineer / System Architect] Technical Point of Contact (TPOC): [Contact Name, Email, Phone]
1. Identification and Significance of the Problem or Opportunity
1.1 The Operational Challenge: Location Leakage and Spoofing in Contested EW
Modern Joint All-Domain Command and Control (JADC2) doctrine relies on high-density deployments of uncrewed autonomous systems (UAS), loitering munitions, and collaborative combat aircraft (CCA). Operating these platforms within contested electromagnetic and anti-access/area-denial (A2/AD) envelopes exposes two critical operational vulnerabilities:
[ Contested Tactical Edge ]
┌─────────────────────────┐      Raw GPS Coordinates / RF Link      ┌─────────────────────────┐
│     Autonomous UAS      │ ───────────────────────────────────────> │  Air Operations Center  │
│  (Sensor/Edge Platform) │ <─────────────────────────────────────── │      (Command Post)     │
└─────────────────────────┘      Interception / Jamming / Spoof      └─────────────────────────┘
                                              │
                                              ▼
                                 [ Hostile EW Intercept ]
                                 • Geolocation Triangulation
                                 • RF Fingerprinting
                                 • Trajectory Prediction

1. RF Signature Exfiltration via Position Telemetry: Conventional tactical geofencing and airspace deconfliction require edge platforms to transmit plaintext coordinates (X, Y, Z, t) back to ground command nodes or neighboring swarm elements. In an active electronic warfare (EW) environment, adversary signals intelligence (SIGINT) systems intercept, triangulate, and target platforms broadcasting raw spatial data over tactical data links (Link 16, MADL, or UHF/VHF).
2. GNSS Spoofing and Unverifiable Dead Reckoning: In GPS-denied environments, platforms transition to dead reckoning, visual-inertial odometry (VIO), or localized terrestrial radio frequency beacons. Adversarial spoofing attacks can inject false coordinate transforms. Current cryptographic mechanisms lack the ability to mathematically prove that a platform is within an authorized operational polygon without revealing exact platform coordinates or sensor telemetry.
1.2 The Innovation: Zero-Knowledge Spatial Verification
The Zero-Knowledge Spatial Verification Protocol (ZKSVP) resolves this tension by decoupling proof of authorized spatial compliance from coordinate disclosure.
By applying pairing-friendly elliptic curve cryptography (BLS12-381) within a resource-constrained no_std embedded core (zksvp-core), an edge platform mathematically proves to a local anchor, swarm peer, or Command and Control (C2) node that:
* Its current 3D position vector (x, y, z) at time t resides strictly within an authorized operational volume \mathcal{V}_{\text{auth}} \subset \mathbb{R}^3.
* Its spatial coordinate assertions are cryptographically bound to hardware root-of-trust sensor measurements.
* Zero side-channel coordinate leakage occurs: An intercepting adversary captures only an elliptic curve group element and zero-knowledge proof transcript, gaining zero bits of information regarding the platform’s actual physical location within the boundary.
2. Technical Approach and Architecture
2.1 Theoretical Framework and Cryptographic Construction
ZKSVP utilizes bilinear pairings over the Barreto-Lynn-Scott curve BLS12-381. Let \mathbb{G}_1 and \mathbb{G}_2 be cyclic subgroups of prime order r, and let \mathbb{G}_T denote the target multiplicative group with bilinear map:
e: \mathbb{G}_1 \times \mathbb{G}_2 \rightarrow \mathbb{G}_T
The operational envelope is discretized into parameterized bounding polyhedra defined by systems of half-spaces:
\mathcal{V}_{\text{auth}} = \bigcap_{i=1}^{m} \left\{ \mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^3 \;\middle\vert{}\; \mathbf{a}_i^T \mathbf{x} + b_i \ge 0 \right\}
                   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                  │               Platform Hardware              │
                  │  ┌────────────────┐      ┌────────────────┐  │
                  │  │ Secure Element │      │  Sensor Fusion │  │
                  │  │  (Root of Trust│      │  (IMU/VIO/GPS) │  │
                  │  └───────┬────────┘      └────────┬───────┘  │
                  └──────────┼────────────────────────┼──────────┘
                             │ Private Key / Scalar   │ Vector (x, y, z, t)
                             ▼                        ▼
                  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                  │                 zksvp-core                   │
                  │  • Fixed-point translation (micromath)       │
                  │  • RFC 9380 SSWU Hash-to-Curve (G1/G2)       │
                  │  • Pedersen Vector Commitments               │
                  │  • Pairing-based Schnorr / Range Proof       │
                  └──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                                         │ Proof π = (A ∈ G1, C ∈ G2, s)
                                         ▼
                              [ Contested Tactical Link ]
                                         │
                                         ▼
                  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                  │             Verifier (C2 / Swarm)            │
                  │  • Multi-Miller Loop: e(A, P2) == e(H, C)    │
                  │  • Output: VALID / INVALID (1 bit)           │
                  └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Step 1: Secure Edge Vector Quantization
Because floating-point calculations are non-deterministic across varied embedded silicon and introduce side-channel vulnerabilities, zksvp-core isolates floating-point approximations (micromath) strictly to non-critical coordinate conditioning.
Spatial coordinates are mapped into finite field elements \mathbb{F}_r via a deterministically scaled fixed-point quantizer:
\hat{x} = \lfloor x \cdot 2^{16} \rfloor \pmod r, \quad \hat{y} = \lfloor y \cdot 2^{16} \rfloor \pmod r, \quad \hat{z} = \lfloor z \cdot 2^{16} \rfloor \pmod r
Step 2: Domain-Separated Hash-to-Curve Attestation
To bind platform time and mission epoch without cross-protocol attacks, the protocol employs RFC 9380 compliant Simplified SWU (SSWU) using ExpandMsgXmd backed by embedded SHA-256:
H_{\mathbb{G}_1} : \{0, 1\}^* \rightarrow \mathbb{G}_1, \quad \text{DST} = \text{"ZKSVP-V01-CS01-BLS12381G1-XMD:SHA-256-SSWU-"}
The mission anchor or C2 broadcasts an epoch beacon T_{\text{epoch}} = (\text{Timestamp} \,\Vert{}\, \text{Nonce}). The edge platform evaluates:
P_{\text{epoch}} = H_{\mathbb{G}_1}(T_{\text{epoch}})
Step 3: Zero-Knowledge Spatial Membership Proof
The platform forms a Pedersen vector commitment to its coordinate vector \mathbf{v} = (\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z}) using curve generator bases (G_1, G_2, G_3, H) \in \mathbb{G}_1^4:
C_{\mathbf{v}} = \hat{x} G_1 + \hat{y} G_2 + \hat{z} G_3 + \gamma H \quad (\text{where } \gamma \stackrel{\$}{\leftarrow} \mathbb{F}_r)
The platform generates non-interactive zero-knowledge range proofs validating that each half-space inequality \mathbf{a}_i^T \mathbf{v} + b_i \ge 0 holds over the committed values, producing proof transcript \pi_{\text{ZKSVP}}.
Step 4: Constant-Time Pairing Verification
The verifier node executes batch verification using a multi-Miller loop and final exponentiation:
e\left(\sum_{k=1}^K \pi_k, \; Q_{\text{base}}\right) \cdot \prod_{j=1}^M e\left(C_j, \; -Q_j\right) \stackrel{?}{=} 1_{\mathbb{G}_T}
If the equation holds, the verifier certifies compliance. The verifier receives zero coordinate data, denying hostile SIGINT nodes interceptable telemetry.
2.2 System Architecture and Embedded Target Execution
The technical baseline is implemented via zksvp-core, an open-architecture Rust library designed for strict Size, Weight, Power, and Cost (SWaP-C) environments.

Perspective of a Fool

Long ago, 

when the boundaries of the world
 were not yet fixed in ink, an ancient willow stood beside a deep and silent well where the cold waters of the northern woods met the broad silt of the southern river. Beneath its boughs was a low table of gray stone, laid as if for travelers who never quite arrive.

There sat the Fool, 
dangling his patched boots above the moss, his chin resting upon a gloved palm. 
Men took him for an idler, for his purse was barren and he carried neither sword nor spool. Yet the Fool was possessed of an insatiable hunger—not for bread or roasted meats, but for the rare wine of human wonder, the sheer, bitter salt of strange deeds and unmeasured passions. He watched the roads not to collect their tolls, but to see how dearly wayfarers paid for their own undoing.

To his feast came the King of Uruk, 
tall as a cedar on Mount Lebanon.
 Upon Gilgamesh 
hung thirty talents of electrum, plates of beaten gold hammered with stars and lions that clanged like iron bells with every tread.
 He set a flagon of pure gold upon the stone and looked upon it as a captain looks upon his shield.
"Let the leaf wither and the cattle perish in the ditch," said Gilgamesh, and his voice was like storm-wind in the reeds. "This metal does not bleed. It is the ancient light of the world taken and made hard. While a man’s name is bound to gold, the worm cannot feast upon his renown."
Then from the roots of the alders hopped a crooked creature whose face was gray as dried ash. 
Rumpelstiltskin brought no flagon;
 he dragged a wheel of seasoned wood and set it spinning with a clacking treadle. Out of his smock he drew dry straw, reaped from harvested fields, dead and yellow as old bone. Yet through his swift, gnarled fingers it ran like water, turning upon the whirring spindle into bright threads of twenty-four-carat wire that coiled into heaps of glittering treasure.
"Listen to the great ox bellow of his renown!" laughed the dwarf, and his mirth was like dry thorns burning under a pot. "You pile up heavy stones to frighten away the dark, King, yet a dead ingot is no more than a leaden stone in a well! To me, gold is but a tether. 
With this shining snare I bought a queen’s crown, and when the season turns, the price of my thread shall be the flesh and blood of her cradle! Gold buys what gold cannot breed!"
Between them sat Enkidu, 
whom the goddess Aruru had pinched from the river silt and quickened with the breath of the wilderness. He wore neither mail nor linen; dry marsh-reeds were tangled in his beard, and his skin was brown as the sun-baked earth. He looked into his rough clay bowl of water and spoke softly.
"You have both looked into the yellow mirror and lost your wits," said Enkidu.
 "When the black fever came upon my limbs, brother, you summoned the smiths to beat forty talents of electrum into the shape of my brow. But did those golden eyes weep when my breath failed? Did those cold lips call you by your secret name? 
On the seventh morning, a worm fell from my nostril into your hand. 
The metal was unblemished, but the man was gone. That which cannot die was never quick with love."
He turned then his dark eyes upon the weaver.
"And you, small shadow of the thicket. You burned the sap out of the corn-stalk to make a halter for an unborn child. 
But a living soul is not a debt to be collected in the night. The queen sent her runner through the hornbeam brake; she watched you leap across your fire; she carried your hidden name into the open day. When the secret is known, the snare falls slack, and the craftsman is swallowed by his own trap."
The Fool leaned forward, his copper bells jingling with a dry, pleasant chime. For him, the gold was neither an idol nor a snare; it was the stone by which he weighed the full, terrible heat of their hearts. He saw the king’s proud armor grow cold and heavy as a slab of gray slate, suffocating the lungs that wore it. He saw the dwarf’s spun thread stretch so taut with malice that it snapped like glass.
"Lo!" cried the Fool, balancing a cracked eggshell on his finger. "The King would turn a brother to stone so he need never weep; the Weaver would turn stone to a child so he need never dwell alone. Both run in circles about the same dark hedge, and neither sees that the gate was open from the first."
Then Gilgamesh looked upon his breastplate, and for the first time he saw that it was not a crown against death, but the gilded gate of a sepulcher. With slow and steady hands, he loosed the buckles and let the heavy electrum fall into the grass, standing bare-chested under the sky. He turned his face toward the baked mud bricks of Uruk—walls raised by common hands, destined to crumble and be renewed, where living men might walk upon the ramparts and shelter their kin.
And from the woodland path there came the faint, clear ringing of a rider’s horn, bearing the true name of the weaver back to the palace gates. At that sound, Rumpelstiltskin shrieked with a fury that split the leaves. Knowing his craft undone and his shadow measured, he stamped his right foot into the earth until it sank to his waist, seized his left leg with both hands, and in his wrath tore himself clean asunder, vanishing beneath the roots where no sun shines.
Enkidu broke a crust of barley bread and shared it with the King.
The Fool took up a single strand of the dwarf’s discarded gold wire, wound it idly about his wrist, and smiled into the gathering dusk. His belly was full of the wonder of the tale.
For the moral of the elder world remains written upon the stone: He who seeks to conquer time with gold makes an ornament of his own grave; he who uses gold to purchase a soul is unmade by the first honest word; but the mud that accepts its own decay becomes the foundation of the city, outlasting both the hoard and the snare.

AN APOCRYPHA OF URUK AND THE DEEP WOODS

THE STONE TABLE OF THE TWO ARCS

T H E F O U R AT T H E TA B L E

Gilgamesh: King of Uruk; seeks to defeat mortality through unrotting gold and eternal monuments.
Rumpelstiltskin: Nameless forest weaver; turns dead straw into gold wire to compel human kinship
through debt.
Enkidu: The wild brother formed from river clay; accepts biological decay as the true condition of love.
The Fool: The court jester of no court; unattached to wealth, debt, or fear, holding the silent balance.

There is an ancient well where the roots of the northern hornbeam drink from the same deep
vein as the southern river. Beside it rests a broad slab of limestone beneath an unmoving willow
whose boughs sweep the moss in rhythmic silence. Upon that stone table, four cups were once
laid to audit the nature of gold.
At the head sat the King of Uruk. His broad shoulders were girded in electrum that flashed
with the cold fire of the sun god Shamash. To Gilgamesh, gold was the solitary constant in a
decomposing universe. Kings died, cattle rotted, and the reeds along the Euphrates withered
before the drought; only the metal refused to bleed. He hoarded it like armor, believing that a
name hammered into bullion was immune to the sickle of time.
To his right, perched upon a three-legged stool of peeled alder, sat the little man of the dark
thicket. Rumpelstiltskin did not venerate the metal. His ash-wood spindle hummed like a hornet
as he fed brittle stalks of wheat through the eyelet, drawing out filaments of twenty-four-carat
thread with reckless contempt. To the weaver, gold was merely bait. Knowing that monarchs
and queens mistook the shine of metal for sovereign power, he manufactured infinite wealth to
purchase the only thing his barren woods could never bear: a living human child.
Across from them sat Enkidu. Fashioned from wet river silt by Aruru’s thumb, he wore no
mail and kept no coins. He smelled of sheepfold, wild melon, and rain. And at the foot of the
table lounged the Fool, balanced upside down upon an overturned chair, juggling two smooth
pebbles and an empty eggshell, unbothered by kingdoms, contracts, or gods.

❖❖❖

The Dialogue of the Hoard and the Net
"The true sovereign yields nothing to the grave," Gilgamesh proclaimed, striking his breastplate
until the valley rang like a bronze gong. "The weak teach their sons so they may pass quietly
into dust, but I am the summit! I permit no successor to eclipse my light. This gold is the

—1—

 signature of an absolute monopoly: it admits no rival, it suffers no decay, and it never steps
aside for what comes next!"
Enkidu dipped his rough earthenware bowl into the well and looked at the King with eyes
that had seen lions whelp in the reeds.
"And because you refuse to step aside," Enkidu answered quietly, "your kingdom dies with
your breath. You cite the law of the shadow—the doctrine that power is preserved only by
clinging to the peak. But the master who builds an eternal fortress of gold produces only a
cemetery. When the fever took me, you summoned fifty smiths to cast my likeness in solid
electrum. You gave my image lapis eyebrows and smoothed its cheeks. But when my breath
failed, did that golden brother weep? Did it wipe the sweat from my brow? On the seventh
morning, a gray worm dropped from my nostril into your open palm. The gold was untouched;
the brother was gone. An unrotting statue is merely an ornament that has forgotten how to
live."
Rumpelstiltskin spat into his spindle, laughing like dry chaff crackling in a baker's fire.
"The King is a fool who confuses an idol with an instrument!" the dwarf cackled. "The dark
master does not worship statues; he cultivates hunger! I took the miller’s daughter when she sat
in terror of the executioner. I was her teacher in the dark! I gave her the yellow metal, and in
exchange, I stamped an impossible lien upon her womb! She was my apprentice in scarcity,
bound to surrender her firstborn—an heir forged in my shadow, destined to inherit my wheel
and command the world!"
Enkidu turned his unblinking gaze upon the creature.
"And how did your apprentice answer your lesson, Weaver?" Enkidu asked softly.
The spindle stuttered on its peg. Rumpelstiltskin’s crooked fingers twitched.
"She surpassed you," Enkidu said. "You taught her that the world is ruled by hidden secrets.
You taught her that he who holds the unmasked name commands the ledger. And so she sent
her scout into your dark grove; she discovered your secret frequency; she spoke your
unvarnished name into the morning light. In the doctrine of tyranny, the apprentice owes the
master only one thing: destruction. She did not pay your debt with a child; she paid it with your
own exposure, rendering your entire empire bankrupt in a single breath."

❖❖❖

The Balance of the Fool
The Fool let his eggshell fall into an empty teacup with a hollow tap. He smiled at the two
masters, his three copper bells chiming in the quiet mountain wind.

—2—

 "The King tried to build a golden bird to flee the worm," whispered the Fool. "The
Weaver tried to buy a warm soul with a cold needle. Two men running in opposite
directions around the same blind mountain, each strangled by the tether of his own
craft."
Gilgamesh sat motionless. He looked down at the electrum plates strapped across his chest.
He saw at last the vanity of the perpetual master. An empire that ends with the emperor is not
an achievement; it is a solitary tomb. He remembered the ramparts of Uruk—not cast in gold,
but raised from river clay, kneaded by mortal hands, dried in the sun, and laid by fathers so
their sons might walk the parapets.
Slowly, the King unbuckled the harness. He laid the heavy breastplate upon the grass, leaving
his chest bare to the morning wind.
"Let the next man build higher," Gilgamesh said, his voice deep and clear. "A true king does
not hoard the summit. He lays the foundation so deep that those who follow may stand upon his
shoulders."
Beneath the table, Rumpelstiltskin heard the distant rustle of the court messenger carrying
his true name back to the palace. The secret was broken; the leverage was gone. In an agony of
thwarted extraction, unable to survive being known, the dwarf drove his foot into the earth and
tore himself in twain, swallowed into the dark silence beneath the roots.
Enkidu smiled, drank his plain water, and offered the King half a crust of barley bread.

T H E F A B L E ' S I N VA R I A N T

The tyrant believes power is kept by making himself an unyielding god;
the dark master believes power is proven only when the student destroys the teacher;
but the wise master knows the ancient truth of the living clay:
True mastery is not the preservation of the throne, nor the survival of a duel in the dark.
True mastery is the willingness to become the foundation stone—so that the apprentice may
surpass the teacher, not by slaying him, but by building upon his dust.

—3—

C O D E X O F L I N E A G E , S U T U R E & T R A N S M U TAT I O N

THE INNER DOCTRINE
On the Rule of Succession, Asymmetric Leverage, and the Living Clay

"The master embodies the power; the apprentice craves it. Yet he who builds a throne of
unrotting gold ensures only his own extinction, for true mastery is not surviving upon an altar,
but becoming the foundation upon which the successor builds higher."

I. The First Axiom: The Tax of Permanence
Matter that refuses to decay is ontologically insolvent. Gold neither oxidizes, rots, nor generates
seed; it stands immune to the thermodynamic cycle. When an authority anchors its legitimacy to
unreactive substance—be it bullion, eternal monuments, or inviolable dogma—it mistakes the
absence of decay for the presence of life.
To hoard matter out of terror is to freeze occurrence into a barren record. An immortal
monument preserves nothing; it merely marks the exact perimeter where living relation ceased.

II. The Dialectic of Dominion: The Sovereign and the Weaver

 III. The Sith Inversion: The Apprentice’s Prerogative
Sith doctrine proclaims that an apprentice must surpass the master, or the line degrades into ash.
Yet tyranny inevitably sabotages its own succession:
