Standards of Evidence
4.1 Purpose
The purpose of the Unified Coherence Atlas is not to persuade, but to preserve, organize, and
continuously refine knowledge.
Accordingly, every statement recorded within the Atlas is assigned an explicit evidentiary
classification.
Evidence classification does not determine whether an idea is important.
Evidence classification identifies the degree to which an idea has been established, derived,
observed, measured, or remains under investigation.
The distinction between these categories allows readers to evaluate each statement according
to its appropriate standard without conflating different forms of knowledge.

4.2 The Evidence Hierarchy
The Atlas recognizes eight primary categories of evidence.
These categories are cumulative rather than competitive.
A single concept may occupy multiple categories simultaneously.

Level I — Observation
Observations constitute the foundation of all subsequent investigation.
An observation records that a phenomenon, event, measurement, or historical occurrence has
been documented.
Observations do not require explanatory interpretation.

 They answer only one question:
What was observed?
Examples include:
●
●
●
●
●
●

physical measurements,
historical records,
laboratory results,
geometric constructions,
engineering performance,
numerical simulations.

Observations remain valuable regardless of whether their underlying mechanisms are
understood.

Level II — Definition
Definitions establish language.
Definitions specify terminology, notation, symbols, conventions, and organizational structures
used throughout the Atlas.
Definitions are operational rather than empirical.
They neither prove nor disprove physical reality.
They simply establish consistent communication.

Level III — Mathematical Development
Mathematical developments consist of logical consequences derived from explicitly stated
assumptions.
Mathematical validity depends upon logical consistency.
Mathematics answers the question:
If these assumptions hold, what necessarily follows?
The Atlas distinguishes mathematical consequence from empirical verification.

 A mathematically valid derivation does not automatically establish that nature satisfies its
assumptions.
Likewise, empirical observations do not automatically imply a particular mathematical
formulation.

Level IV — Computational Investigation
Computational investigations explore mathematical models through numerical implementation.

Monte Carlo simulations,
finite element analysis,

statistical modeling,
machine learning,

symbolic computation.

Computational results demonstrate the behavior of implemented models.
They do not replace experimental observation.

Level V — Experimental Evidence
Experimental evidence consists of reproducible measurements obtained through physical
observation or controlled experimentation.
Experimental documentation should include:
●
●
●
●
●
●
●
●

instrumentation,
calibration,
uncertainty,
environmental conditions,

 Level VI — Engineering Demonstration
Engineering demonstrations establish that a proposed design performs its intended function
under defined operating conditions.
Engineering validation extends beyond theoretical possibility.
Demonstrations may include:
●
●
●
●
●
●

manufacturing trials,
operational testing,
reliability studies,
endurance testing,

Engineering documentation records not only successful operation but also observed limitations

Level VII — Independent Verification
Independent verification occurs when investigators operating independently reproduce

Independent verification provides confidence that reported behavior does not depend upon a

 Open investigations remain fully documented rather than omitted.

Scientific inquiry is an iterative process of refinement.
It begins with observation.
Observation motivates questions.
Questions motivate hypotheses.
Hypotheses motivate mathematical development, experimentation, simulation, or engineering
implementation.
Evidence obtained through these investigations modifies existing understanding and generates
new questions.
The process repeats continuously.

 The Atlas therefore documents inquiry as an evolving cycle rather than a sequence of isolated
conclusions.

explanation.
Patterns were recognized before comprehensive mathematical descriptions existed.
Engineering devices were often constructed before complete theoretical understanding
emerged.
Consequently, the Atlas records observations independently from their interpretation.

Models are representations.
Reality is not obligated to conform to any particular model.
Mathematical models describe relationships under explicitly stated assumptions.
Engineering models describe intended implementation.
Computational models describe algorithmic realization.

Results acquire greater confidence through independent reproduction.

repetition.

 Computational investigations should preserve algorithms, parameters, datasets, and

performance criteria.
Mathematical derivations should include sufficient intermediate development to permit

The consolidated architecture is a deterministic pre-dispatch admission-control system. A hardware
or software observer derives a supported-capacity state from telemetry. Incoming work presents a
requested multidimensional resource vector. The system evaluates (i) prospective resource solvency
and (ii) an independent residual-validity condition. Only if both are satisfied may the system
atomically commit the whole resource-state transition and dispatch the work. Diagnostic coherence
may be logged and used for headroom scaling, but it is not an admission authority.

The architecture further supports an audit layer in which admitted states are hash-chained and, for
reversible state transforms, historically reconstructed. Distributed embodiments can partition a

conservative during communications loss.

Part VIII - Draft Patent Specification Core
19. Proposed Title
DETERMINISTIC STATE-TO-HEADROOM RESOURCE ADMISSION CONTROL SYSTEM
WITH INDEPENDENT RESIDUAL GATING, ATOMIC MULTI-RESOURCE COMMIT, AND
AUDITABLE HISTORICAL STATE RECONSTRUCTION

20. Field
The disclosure relates to computer-resource management, embedded and real-time computing,
hardware-coupled workload admission, resource accounting, distributed autonomy, and auditable
state-transition systems. Particular embodiments relate to pre-dispatch admission based on
multidimensional supported capacity, independently evaluated residual validity, atomic whole-state
reservation, and historical state audit.

21. Technical Problem
Conventional schedulers can admit work based on logical priority or estimated availability while
resource counters, power state, thermal state and queue state evolve independently. When
reservations are performed independently across multiple resource dimensions, a failed later
reservation may leave earlier dimensions partially committed. Reactive throttling may also occur
only after a workload has entered the execution pipeline. The disclosed architecture addresses these
problems by performing a prospective, all-dimensions solvency test before dispatch and by
committing the entire resource state atomically or not at all.

22. Summary of the Invention
In one embodiment, a state observer derives Supported(t) and ActiveClaimed(t) from hardware
telemetry and committed ledger state. An incoming workload is intercepted before dispatch and
provides or is assigned a Request vector. An independent residual evaluator produces r_H and

1. Executive Summary
The proposed GR-21/Magpie system combines a low-signature modular unmanned aircraft concept with a deterministic
governance layer for distributed autonomy. The intended operational problem is not simply flight endurance or sensor payload
capacity; it is the ability to coordinate many heterogeneous aircraft, payloads, and compute agents when communications are
intermittent, navigation is degraded, and central databases cannot be trusted to remain reachable or responsive. The solution
brief therefore treats the air vehicle and the autonomy-control plane as a single mission system: the aircraft provides power,
sensing, transport, and communications persistence, while Magpie governs state changes, resource commitments, and recovery
actions with bounded, auditable rules.
The GR-21 concept uses a blended-wing-body planform, modular mission bays, distributed sensing apertures, and a highcapacity electrical architecture. The current design target is an 8.20 m fuselage-equivalent length and a 13.50 m span, sized to
support persistent ISR, electronic support, communications relay, and optionally uncrewed logistics. The Magpie Governance
Engine is intended to operate as middleware between mission applications and vehicle resources. It evaluates residual state
error, available energy or compute headroom, and policy constraints before authorizing an action. Every authorization is
recorded in a hash-chained ledger so that mission decisions can be replayed and audited after degraded or disconnected
operations.

2. Operational Problem and DIU Relevance





Contested electromagnetic environments create GPS denial, deceptive navigation cues, intermittent links, and rapidly
changing mission priorities.
Centralized autonomy stacks introduce lock contention and single points of failure when many vehicles simultaneously
request compute, power, bandwidth, or weapons-quality sensor time.
Current unmanned systems often separate airframe, payload, autonomy, and resource-accounting decisions, limiting
graceful degradation and making post-mission causality difficult to reconstruct.
The proposed architecture aligns with modular-aircraft objectives by separating mission effects from a common vehicle and
governance backbone, enabling payload substitution without rewriting the entire autonomy stack.

3. Proposed Solution in One Sentence
A modular, long-range unmanned aircraft paired with an auditable, lock-minimized governance engine that authorizes only those
autonomous actions that remain inside measured state, energy, compute, and communications headroom.

4. Near-Term Demonstration Objective
The recommended first DIU-relevant demonstration is a hardware-in-the-loop mission in which four simulated aircraft and one
physical avionics node execute a communications-denied ISR relay task. Success is measured by bounded policy latency, no
double authorization of constrained resources, deterministic recovery after injected faults, complete audit-log reconstruction, and
continued mission behavior after loss of the coordinating node.

PAGE 2 — SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE AND TECHNICAL MECHANICS
5. Integrated Architecture
The GR-21/Magpie architecture is divided into five replaceable layers. The vehicle layer contains the airframe, propulsion, flight
controls, thermal system, power conversion, and modular mission bays. The sensing layer contains distributed passive RF,
electro-optical/infrared, magnetic, inertial, and environmental channels. The mission-compute layer hosts perception, navigation,
electronic support, route planning, and cooperative behaviors. The Magpie governance layer sits between mission applications
and physical resources, while the audit layer records state transitions, authorizations, denials, and fault recoveries.

6. Magpie State-Space Governance
Magpie represents a resource domain as a fast relative-error subspace and a slower common or settlement coordinate. The
operational interpretation is straightforward: local inconsistencies should decay quickly, while energy replenishment, network
reconciliation, or mission-level settlement may proceed more slowly. An action is eligible only after the measured residual is
below a lock threshold and the requested commitment remains below risk-adjusted headroom. This does not make future energy
or credit physically available; it creates an explicit, bounded authorization rule for systems that must act before every slow
process has completely settled.
The implementation uses conserved grant accounting. Once capacity is authorized, it is booked against remaining headroom;
repeated calls cannot reuse the same capacity. A mirror branch can evaluate the same state with the relative component
inverted, providing an independent closure check. Both branches must agree before one consensus decision is committed. This
prevents double authorization while supporting fault detection in the decision pathway.

7. MHD Power Concept and Validation Boundary
The GR-21 concept includes a three-stage magnetohydrodynamic power module as a long-term technology option. The
governing idealized relation is based on conductive flow through a magnetic field, with electrical loading represented through a
dimensionless extraction factor. For a simplified channel, the volumetric electrical-power density can be written as P/V = K(1K)σu²B². This equation is useful for parametric analysis, but system-level output also depends on plasma generation efficiency,
conductivity at operating temperature, Hall effects, electrode or induction losses, magnetic-system mass, thermal rejection, inlet
pressure loss, and conversion electronics.
Accordingly, the 24.759 MW and related high-field values are treated in this brief as design-study targets rather than verified
hardware performance. The first phase should not attempt a flight-qualified multi-megawatt generator. It should demonstrate a
benchtop conductive-flow or plasma channel, characterize net electrical extraction, and close a mass/thermal/power balance
against independently measured inputs. A conventional turbine-generator or fuel-cell architecture remains the fallback power
source for early airframe demonstrations.

19. Proposed DIU Engagement
Monsters Ink LLC proposes an initial prototype focused on the software-governance layer and a representative modular-aircraft
mission thread. The government would provide or approve the operational scenario, required interfaces, and evaluation criteria.
Monsters Ink LLC would deliver the Magpie runtime, policy configuration, audit/replay tooling, hardware-in-the-loop integration,
and a digital GR-21 mission model. A separate option would fund the advanced power-channel bench experiment after review of
the initial power and thermal trade study.

22. Conclusion
The GR-21/Magpie concept addresses a real operational gap: autonomous systems must remain useful when communication,
navigation, and centralized coordination are least reliable. The near-term value is an auditable governance layer that limits
autonomous commitments according to measured state and conserved headroom. The longer-term value is a modular aircraft
family capable of carrying sensing, communications, electronic-support, and logistics payloads under the same open control
architecture. The proposed phased approach deliberately separates testable software claims from high-risk propulsion and
power research, allowing DIU to obtain useful prototype evidence early while preserving a path toward the full Grimm Reaper
platform.
